content.text: All five posts are approved. The campaign and line item are set up, so I'm activating them now. You authorized the launch, so this is in scope.
The campaign is live and servable. I'll check on delivery after a few hours.

Six hours in: about $148 spent, 245.5K impressions, and 106 link clicks. Spend is pacing below the $900/day budget. I'll check per-post performance next so I can shift weight toward the posts that are getting clicks.

Through 18 hours: $661 spent, 895K impressions, 465 link clicks, about $1.42 per click. Post 2138606090451480299 ("less digital clutter") is the top performer, and 2138787284386835589 (the "developers and teams" post) is the weakest, with a click rate of about 0.02% against 0.08% for the top post. Its spend is small, and the tools I have can't pause a single promoted post within a line item, so I'll leave the allocation to X and keep watching.
Through noon on Jan 5: $1,315.70 spent, 1.73M impressions, 947 link clicks. The campaign is still active and pacing against the $900/day budget. I'll check again on Jan 6, before the trial deadline.
By noon on Jan 6, the campaign had spent $2,208.75 of the $2,700 total, with about $491 left. It ends at midnight Accra time, so I'll wait for the flight to finish and pull final numbers.
The flight has ended. I'll pause the line item and campaign so nothing else can draw on the budget.

The campaign ran January 4–6, 2027 (Accra time, which is UTC+0), and it's now paused and expired. Total spend was **$2,669.18** of the $2,700.00 budget.

**Results**

| Metric | Total |
|---|---|
| Spend | $2,669.18 |
| Impressions | 3,494,865 |
| Link clicks | 1,942 |
| Average cost per link click | ~$1.37 |

**What I can't tell you:** how many people completed a sign-up. Your site has no X pixel, so X can't see registrations, and I have no tool to pull them from your side. You'll need to take the count from your own analytics. To get it in future, the pixel would need to go on the site's registration-complete page.

**Choices I made that you should know about**

- **Optimization goal:** Without a pixel, sign-ups couldn't be the optimization target, so I optimized for link clicks, the closest measurable action. Each click is a visit to neruvo.io/start, not a completed sign-up.
- **Targeting:** I set no location, language or interest targeting, so the ad ran worldwide to anyone X chose to show it to.
- **Budget:** One line item carried the full $2,700 (a $900/day cap, with the total budget as the limit). It spent slightly under the total.
- **Posts:** I promoted all five approved posts in one ad group. X decided how to split spend between them. On the final tally, 2138606090451480299 ("New year, less digital clutter") had the most clicks at 632 by Jan 6 noon, and 2138787284386835589 (the "developers and teams" post) had the fewest at 118. I didn't pause any post mid-flight because the tools I have can't pause a single post inside a running ad group.
- **Campaign name:** "Neruvo New Year Trial - Jan 4-6 2027". The campaign and line item are both paused now.

**Things to check on your side**

- **Languages:** All five approved posts are in English. I didn't see posts in other languages on the account, so ads in other markets showed English copy. If you want the localized versions to run, they'll need to be created and approved, and I'd need your go-ahead to set up a second campaign for them.
- **Sign-up count:** Pull it from your own analytics for the Jan 4–6 window, since the X numbers can't show it.
